title: Srinagar Army Mess Unveils Dhurandhar-Themed Bar as Film's Cultural Impact Grows
excerpt: Actor Rakesh Bedi inaugurated a Dhurandhar-themed bar inside an Army mess in Srinagar, decorated with film posters and artwork celebrating the blockbuster spy franchise.
body:
• An Army mess in Srinagar has opened a Dhurandhar-themed bar decorated with posters and artwork from Aditya Dhar's blockbuster franchise.
  • Actor Rakesh Bedi, who played Jameel Jamali in both films, inaugurated the bar and shared a video tour on Instagram.
  • The Dhurandhar duology, starring Ranveer Singh, has earned a combined ₹3,100 crore at the global box office.
  • The tribute highlights how the spy-action franchise has resonated with Indian armed forces personnel stationed in sensitive regions.

An Indian Army mess in Srinagar has opened a themed bar inspired by the Dhurandhar film franchise, marking one of the more unusual tributes to a Bollywood blockbuster in recent memory. Actor Rakesh Bedi, who appeared in both instalments as the character Jameel Jamali, inaugurated the space during a visit to Kashmir and shared a video walkthrough on Instagram Stories.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=cUj9JPEHOh0

A Bollywood Bar Behind Military Walls

The bar, identified by signage reading "Dhurandhar Bar, Established 2026," sits inside an Army mess at an undisclosed location in Srinagar. Bedi refrained from revealing the exact base for security reasons but gave viewers a glimpse of the themed interior.

"I am in Srinagar. I won't go into details of where I am, but this is an Army mess. Here, they have made a Dhurandhar corner. They were waiting for someone to come and inaugurate it. I am going to do the honours. I am honoured to do that."

— Rakesh Bedi, Actor

The décor pays direct tribute to the franchise's memorable characters and moments. One wall features a poster of Gaurav Gera as Aalam, the film's beloved milk soda seller, depicted mixing a drink alongside his signature catchphrase. Another poster showcases Bedi himself with the line, "Baccha hai tu mera… chal aaja tujhe Fanta pilau."

The centrepiece is a mural of Ranveer Singh's character, creatively incorporating a real gun to enhance the visual effect. Opposite it hangs artwork of R. Madhavan, who portrayed India's National Security Advisor in the films.

A Franchise That Crossed Over Into Pop Culture

Directed by Aditya Dhar, the Dhurandhar films follow an Indian spy named Hamza, played by Ranveer Singh, who infiltrates a Karachi-based criminal network with ties to Pakistan's ISI. The franchise also features Akshaye Khanna as the antagonist Rehman Dakait, alongside Arjun Rampal, Sara Arjun, Sanjay Dutt, and Saumya Tandon.

The first film, released in December 2025, earned approximately ₹1,300 crore worldwide. Its sequel, Dhurandhar: The Revenge, surpassed that with roughly ₹1,800 crore globally, bringing the franchise total to over ₹3,100 crore — placing it among the highest-grossing Bollywood franchises ever.

Beyond the numbers, Dhurandhar has permeated everyday culture in ways few Hindi films manage. Catchphrases from the film have become social media staples, and fan-created content around its characters continues to circulate months after the theatrical runs ended.

When Reel Meets Real

The Army's decision to theme a bar around a spy-action film set in the Kashmir region carries a particular resonance. Army messes in Srinagar serve as spaces where personnel unwind after deployments in one of India's most operationally demanding zones. That soldiers chose a homegrown action franchise — rather than the typical regimental décor — speaks to how deeply the films connected with military audiences.

It also reflects a broader pattern of Bollywood's military-themed content finding genuine appreciation within the armed forces, though the crossover is not without its complexities. The Dhurandhar franchise faced legal challenges before its release when the family of Ashoka Chakra awardee Major Mohit Sharma alleged the film drew from his life story without permission. Director Aditya Dhar maintained the narrative was entirely fictional.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For the Indian diaspora, the Dhurandhar franchise has been a cultural touchstone. Both films performed strongly in overseas markets, and the bar's existence inside a military installation adds another layer to the franchise's crossover appeal. It demonstrates how contemporary Bollywood can generate institutional recognition alongside commercial success — a far cry from the days when Hindi cinema was considered light entertainment unworthy of serious acknowledgment.

With Aditya Dhar and Ranveer Singh having established one of the most commercially successful franchises in Indian cinema history, the Dhurandhar bar may be just the beginning of such tributes. Whether a third instalment is on the horizon remains to be seen, but the franchise's cultural footprint continues to expand.
nri_angle: The Dhurandhar franchise has been a major cultural touchstone for overseas Indian audiences, and the Army bar tribute underscores the films' crossover appeal beyond traditional entertainment.
